- [run_pretrained_openfold.py:63-175]()
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:864-914]()
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:111-130]()

## MSA and Template Processing

Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) and structural templates are critical components of AlphaFold's accuracy. OpenFold provides robust processing for both:

### MSA Processing

MSAs are generated using tools like Jackhmmer and HHblits, then processed to extract evolutionarily relevant information:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "MSA Generation"
        FASTA["FASTA sequence"]
        Jackhmmer["Jackhmmer search"]
        HHblits["HHblits search"]
        MSA_Files["MSA files (.sto, .a3m)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MSA Processing"
        ParseMSA["Parse MSA files"]
        DeduplicateMSA["Deduplicate sequences"]
        RemoveEmpty["Remove empty columns"]
        ExtractFeatures["Extract MSA features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MSA Transformations"
        SampleMSA["Sample MSA sequences"]
        MaskedMSA["Make masked MSA"]
        MSACluster["Nearest neighbor clusters"]
        CreateFeat["Create MSA features"]
    end
    
    FASTA --> Jackhmmer
    FASTA --> HHblits
    Jackhmmer --> MSA_Files
    HHblits --> MSA_Files
    
    MSA_Files --> ParseMSA
    ParseMSA --> DeduplicateMSA
    DeduplicateMSA --> RemoveEmpty
    RemoveEmpty --> ExtractFeatures
    
    ExtractFeatures --> SampleMSA
    SampleMSA --> MaskedMSA
    MaskedMSA --> MSACluster
    MSACluster --> CreateFeat
```

Sources:
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:477-562](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:224-259](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)
- [openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py:75-125](openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py)
- [openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py:129-183](openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py)
- [openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py:257-294](openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py)

Key MSA processing steps include:
1. Sequence alignment using external tools
2. Parsing alignment files (.sto, .a3m)
3. Deduplication and filtering
4. Feature extraction (insertions, deletions, conservation)
5. Sampling and cropping for fixed-size inputs
6. BERT-style masking for masked MSA prediction

### Template Processing

Template structures are found and processed to provide structural priors:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Template Search"
        MSA["MSA data"]
        HHsearch["HHsearch (monomer)"]
        HMMsearch["HMMsearch (multimer)"]
        Hits["Template hits"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Template Processing"
        FilterHits["Filter by date/quality"]
        RankHits["Rank by E-value"]
        SubsampleHits["Subsample hits"]
        AlignHits["Align to query"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Template Featurization"
        FeaturizeTemplate["Template featurization"]
        BuildFeatures["Build template features"]
        CropTemplates["Crop templates"]
    end
    
    MSA --> HHsearch
    MSA --> HMMsearch
    HHsearch --> Hits
    HMMsearch --> Hits
    
    Hits --> FilterHits
    FilterHits --> RankHits
    RankHits --> SubsampleHits
    SubsampleHits --> AlignHits
    
    AlignHits --> FeaturizeTemplate
    FeaturizeTemplate --> BuildFeatures
    BuildFeatures --> CropTemplates
```

Sources:
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:500-518](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:46-63](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:159-167](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:405-413](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)

Template processing includes:
1. Finding template structures using HHsearch (monomer) or HMMsearch (multimer)
2. Filtering by release date and quality metrics
3. Ranking and selecting the top templates
4. Aligning templates to the target sequence
5. Extracting template features (atom positions, amino acid types, masks)

## Multimer Data Processing

For multi-chain proteins (multimers), OpenFold implements specialized processing:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Chain Processing"
        ReadChains["Read individual chains"]
        ProcessChains["Process each chain"]
        ChainFeatures["Chain features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MSA Pairing"
        CreatePaired["Create paired features"]
        DeduplicateUnpaired["Deduplicate unpaired sequences"]
        PairRows["Reorder paired rows"]
    end

        MergeHomomers["Merge homomers"]
        MergeFeatures["Merge chain features"]
        ConcatFeatures["Concatenate paired/unpaired features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-Processing"
        CorrectFeats["Correct post-merged features"]
        CropChains["Crop chains"]
        FilterFeatures["Filter features"]
    end
    
    ReadChains --> ProcessChains
    ProcessChains --> ChainFeatures
    
    ChainFeatures --> CreatePaired
    CreatePaired --> DeduplicateUnpaired
    DeduplicateUnpaired --> PairRows
    
    PairRows --> MergeHomomers
    MergeHomomers --> MergeFeatures
```

Sources:
- [openfold/data/msa_pairing.py:56-88](openfold/data/msa_pairing.py)
- [openfold/data/msa_pairing.py:181-232](openfold/data/msa_pairing.py)
- [openfold/data/msa_pairing.py:356-457](openfold/data/msa_pairing.py)
- [openfold/data/feature_processing_multimer.py:50-83](openfold/data/feature_processing_multimer.py)
- [openfold/data/feature_processing_multimer.py:87-116](openfold/data/feature_processing_multimer.py)

Key multimer processing steps include:
1. Processing each chain individually
2. Pairing MSA sequences across chains based on species
3. Merging identical chains (homomers) efficiently
4. Combining features from all chains
5. Special handling for template features across chains
6. Cropping the combined features to manageable sizes

## Data Transformations

The data undergoes various transformations to prepare it for model input:

### Non-ensembled Transforms

Applied once to the input data:
- Converting data types (e.g., 64-bit integers)
- Creating MSA profiles
- Creating target features
- Making atom masks

### Ensembled Transforms

Applied multiple times for recycling:
- MSA sampling
- MSA masking for BERT-style training
- MSA clustering
- Cropping to fixed size

These transformations are implemented in `data_transforms.py` and `data_transforms_multimer.py`.

Sources:
- [openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py:36-45](openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py)
- [openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py:48-113](openfold/data/input_pipeline_multimer.py)
- [openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py:75-125](openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py)
- [openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py:257-294](openfold/data/data_transforms_multimer.py)

## Training Data Handling

For training, the pipeline includes additional components for data filtering, batching, and augmentation:

### Filtering

Training data undergoes both deterministic and stochastic filtering:

```python
# Deterministic filters
resolution_filter(resolution, max_resolution)
aa_count_filter(seqs, max_single_aa_prop)

# Stochastic filters
# Prefer diverse sequences (inversely proportional to cluster size)
# Prefer medium-length chains
```

### Batching and Recycling

The `OpenFoldDataLoader` handles batching and adds batch properties like recycling iterations:

```python
# Add number of recycling iterations
recycling_probs = [1. / (max_iters + 1) for _ in range(max_iters + 1)]
# Or use the maximum number of recycling iterations by default
recycling_probs = [0. for _ in range(max_iters + 1)]
recycling_probs[-1] = 1.
```

Sources:
- [openfold/data/data_modules.py:507-532](openfold/data/data_modules.py)
- [openfold/data/data_modules.py:560-595](openfold/data/data_modules.py)
- [openfold/data/data_modules.py:708-713](openfold/data/data_modules.py)
- [openfold/data/data_modules.py:762-845](openfold/data/data_modules.py)

## Summary

The OpenFold data processing pipeline is a sophisticated system that:
1. Loads protein data from various formats
2. Generates and processes MSAs and templates
3. Extracts and transforms features for model input
4. Handles both monomer and multimer proteins
5. Provides specialized functionality for training data

This pipeline is critical for achieving high-quality protein structure predictions, as it prepares the complex evolutionary and structural information needed by the model.

Sources:
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)
- [openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py](openfold/data/feature_pipeline.py)

# Page: Data Pipeline and Feature Generation

# Data Pipeline and Feature Generation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py](openfold/data/data_pipeline.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the data processing pipeline that converts raw biological inputs (FASTA sequences, mmCIF/PDB structures) into feature dictionaries suitable for model inference and training. The pipeline orchestrates MSA generation, template search, and feature extraction through the `DataPipeline` and `AlignmentRunner` classes.

For information about data transformations applied after feature generation (sampling, masking, cropping), see [Data Transforms and Augmentation](#6.2). For details on MSA generation tools and template search, see [MSA and Template Processing](#6.3). For multimer-specific processing including chain pairing, see [Multimer-Specific Processing](#6.4).

---

## System Overview

The data pipeline consists of three major stages:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Stage 1: Alignment Generation"
        FASTA["FASTA Input"]
        AR["AlignmentRunner"]
        MSA_FILES["MSA Files<br/>(*.sto, *.a3m)"]
        TEMPLATE_FILES["Template Files<br/>(*.hhr, hmm_output.sto)"]
        
        FASTA --> AR
        AR --> MSA_FILES
        AR --> TEMPLATE_FILES
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Feature Extraction"
        DP["DataPipeline"]
        PARSERS["Parsers<br/>parse_stockholm<br/>parse_a3m<br/>parse_hhr"]
        TF["TemplateFeaturizer"]
        
        MSA_FILES --> PARSERS
        TEMPLATE_FILES --> PARSERS
        PARSERS --> DP
        TF --> DP
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Feature Dict Assembly"
        SEQ_FEAT["Sequence Features<br/>aatype, residue_index"]
        MSA_FEAT["MSA Features<br/>msa, deletion_matrix"]
        TEMPL_FEAT["Template Features<br/>positions, aatype"]
        EMBED_FEAT["Embeddings<br/>seq_embedding (optional)"]
        
        DP --> SEQ_FEAT
        DP --> MSA_FEAT
        DP --> TEMPL_FEAT
        DP --> EMBED_FEAT
    end
    
    FINAL["FeatureDict<br/>Ready for FeaturePipeline"]
    
    SEQ_FEAT --> FINAL
    MSA_FEAT --> FINAL
    TEMPL_FEAT --> FINAL
    EMBED_FEAT --> FINAL
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:1-1161](), [run_pretrained_openfold.py:63-170]()

## DataPipeline Class

The `DataPipeline` class is the central orchestrator that converts alignment outputs and structural data into standardized feature dictionaries.

### Class Structure

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DataPipeline {
        +TemplateHitFeaturizer template_featurizer
        +process_fasta(fasta_path, alignment_dir) FeatureDict
        +process_mmcif(mmcif, alignment_dir) FeatureDict
        +process_multiseq_fasta(fasta_path, super_alignment_dir) FeatureDict
        -_parse_msa_data(alignment_dir) Mapping
        -_parse_template_hit_files(alignment_dir) Mapping
        -_process_msa_feats(alignment_dir) FeatureDict
        -_process_seqemb_features(alignment_dir) FeatureDict
        -_get_msas(alignment_dir) List[Msa]
    }
    
    class DataPipelineMultimer {
        +DataPipeline monomer_data_pipeline
        +process_fasta(fasta_path, alignment_dir) FeatureDict
    }
    
    class TemplateHitFeaturizer {
        <<interface>>
        +get_templates(query_sequence, hits) TemplateSearchResult
    }
    
    class HhsearchHitFeaturizer {
        +str mmcif_dir
        +datetime max_template_date
        +int max_hits
        +get_templates() TemplateSearchResult
    }
    
    class HmmsearchHitFeaturizer {
        +str mmcif_dir
        +datetime max_template_date
        +int max_hits
        +get_templates() TemplateSearchResult
    }
    
    class CustomHitFeaturizer {
        +str mmcif_dir
        +str kalign_binary_path
        +get_templates() TemplateSearchResult
    }
    
    DataPipeline --> TemplateHitFeaturizer
    DataPipelineMultimer --> DataPipeline
    TemplateHitFeaturizer <|-- HhsearchHitFeaturizer
    TemplateHitFeaturizer <|-- HmmsearchHitFeaturizer
    TemplateHitFeaturizer <|-- CustomHitFeaturizer
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:706-915](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:916-1161](), [openfold/data/templates.py:930-1145]()

### Main Processing Methods

The `DataPipeline` class provides three main entry points:

| Method | Input | Purpose | Used For |
|--------|-------|---------|----------|
| `process_fasta()` | FASTA file + alignment directory | Process single-chain sequences | Monomer inference, SoloSeq mode |
| `process_mmcif()` | mmCIF object + alignment directory | Process structure with alignments | Training on PDB structures |
| `process_multiseq_fasta()` | Multi-sequence FASTA + alignments | Process multiple chains | Legacy multi-chain (pre-multimer) |

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:864-914](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:916-999](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:1001-1046]()

## AlignmentRunner

The `AlignmentRunner` class orchestrates external bioinformatics tools to generate MSAs and template search results.

### Tool Configuration

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "AlignmentRunner Configuration"
        AR["AlignmentRunner"]
        
        subgraph "MSA Search Tools"
            JACK_U90["jackhmmer_uniref90_runner<br/>Jackhmmer vs UniRef90"]
            JACK_MGN["jackhmmer_mgnify_runner<br/>Jackhmmer vs MGnify"]
            JACK_BFD["jackhmmer_small_bfd_runner<br/>Jackhmmer vs small BFD"]
            HHB["hhblits_bfd_unirefclust_runner<br/>HHBlits vs BFD+UniRef30/UniClust30"]
            JACK_UNI["jackhmmer_uniprot_runner<br/>Jackhmmer vs UniProt (multimer)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Template Search"
            HHS["HHSearch<br/>vs PDB70"]
            HMS["Hmmsearch<br/>vs pdb_seqres"]
        end
        
        AR --> JACK_U90
        AR --> JACK_MGN
        AR --> JACK_BFD
        AR --> HHB
        AR --> JACK_UNI
        AR --> HHS
        AR --> HMS
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        U90_OUT["uniref90_hits.sto"]
        MGN_OUT["mgnify_hits.sto"]
        BFD_OUT["bfd_*_hits.a3m / small_bfd_hits.sto"]
        UNI_OUT["uniprot_hits.sto"]
        TEMPL_OUT["output.hhr / hmmsearch_output.sto"]
    end
    
    JACK_U90 --> U90_OUT
    JACK_MGN --> MGN_OUT
    JACK_BFD --> BFD_OUT
    HHB --> BFD_OUT
    JACK_UNI --> UNI_OUT
    HHS --> TEMPL_OUT
    HMS --> TEMPL_OUT
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:334-476]()

### AlignmentRunner.run() Workflow

The `run()` method executes the full alignment pipeline:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant AR as AlignmentRunner
    participant J as Jackhmmer
    participant H as HHBlits/HHSearch/Hmmsearch
    participant FS as File System
    
    C->>AR: run(fasta_path, output_dir)
    
    alt UniRef90 Search
        AR->>J: query(fasta_path, max_sto_sequences)
        J->>FS: Write uniref90_hits.sto
        
        alt Template Search Enabled
            AR->>AR: deduplicate_stockholm_msa()
            AR->>AR: remove_empty_columns_from_stockholm_msa()
            
            alt HHSearch (monomer)
                AR->>H: query(template_msa, output_dir)
                H->>FS: Write output.hhr
            else Hmmsearch (multimer)
                AR->>H: query(template_msa, output_dir)
                H->>FS: Write hmmsearch_output.sto
            end
        end
    end
    
    alt MGnify Search
        AR->>J: query(fasta_path, max_sto_sequences)
        J->>FS: Write mgnify_hits.sto
    end
    
    alt BFD Search
        alt use_small_bfd
            AR->>J: query(fasta_path)
            J->>FS: Write small_bfd_hits.sto
        else use_full_bfd
            AR->>H: query(fasta_path)
            H->>FS: Write bfd_uniref_hits.a3m / bfd_uniclust_hits.a3m
        end
    end
    
    alt UniProt Search (multimer only)
        AR->>J: query(fasta_path, max_sto_sequences)
        J->>FS: Write uniprot_hits.sto
    end
    
    AR->>C: Return (all files written)
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:477-563]()

### Integration with Inference

In the inference script, alignment generation is handled by `precompute_alignments()`:

```mermaid
graph TB
    FASTA["FASTA File(s)"]
    CHECK{"use_precomputed_<br/>alignments?"}
    
    subgraph "Alignment Generation"
        CREATE_AR["Create AlignmentRunner<br/>with tool binaries & DBs"]
        SEL_SEARCHER{"multimer<br/>mode?"}
        HMS_S["Hmmsearch<br/>template_searcher"]
        HHS_S["HHSearch<br/>template_searcher"]
        RUN["alignment_runner.run()<br/>fasta_path, output_dir"]
    end
    
    ALIGN_DIR["Alignment Directory<br/>per-sequence subdirs"]
    
    FASTA --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|No| CREATE_AR
    CREATE_AR --> SEL_SEARCHER
    SEL_SEARCHER -->|Yes| HMS_S
    SEL_SEARCHER -->|No| HHS_S
    HMS_S --> RUN
    HHS_S --> RUN
    RUN --> ALIGN_DIR
    CHECK -->|Yes| ALIGN_DIR
```

**Sources**: [run_pretrained_openfold.py:63-123]()

## Feature Generation Components

### Sequence Features

Basic sequence-level features are created by `make_sequence_features()`:

| Feature Name | Shape | Type | Description |
|--------------|-------|------|-------------|
| `aatype` | `(num_res, 21)` | `float32` | One-hot encoded amino acid types |
| `residue_index` | `(num_res,)` | `int32` | Residue indices (0 to num_res-1) |
| `seq_length` | `(num_res,)` | `int32` | Sequence length broadcast to all residues |
| `sequence` | `(1,)` | `object` | Raw amino acid sequence (encoded bytes) |
| `domain_name` | `(1,)` | `object` | Sequence description/ID (encoded bytes) |
| `between_segment_residues` | `(num_res,)` | `int32` | Zeros (used in multimer for chain breaks) |

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:111-130]()

### MSA Features

MSA features are constructed by `make_msa_features()` from parsed MSA objects:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input: List of Msa Objects"
        MSA1["Msa 1<br/>sequences<br/>deletion_matrix<br/>descriptions"]
        MSA2["Msa 2"]
        MSAN["Msa N"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        DEDUP["Deduplicate sequences<br/>across all MSAs"]
        CONVERT["Convert to integer encoding<br/>HHBLITS_AA_TO_ID"]
        EXTRACT["Extract species identifiers<br/>from descriptions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Features"
        MSA_FEAT["msa<br/>(num_alignments, num_res)<br/>int32"]
        DEL_FEAT["deletion_matrix_int<br/>(num_alignments, num_res)<br/>int32"]
        NUM_FEAT["num_alignments<br/>(num_res,)<br/>int32"]
        SPEC_FEAT["msa_species_identifiers<br/>(num_alignments,)<br/>object"]
    end
    
    MSA1 --> DEDUP
    MSA2 --> DEDUP
    MSAN --> DEDUP
    DEDUP --> CONVERT
    DEDUP --> EXTRACT
    CONVERT --> MSA_FEAT
    CONVERT --> DEL_FEAT
    CONVERT --> NUM_FEAT
    EXTRACT --> SPEC_FEAT
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:224-261]()

### Template Features

Template features are generated through a multi-step process involving alignment to query and extraction of structural information:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input"
        HITS["Template Hits<br/>from HHSearch/Hmmsearch"]
        QUERY["Query Sequence"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Template Featurizer"
        PREFILT["_prefilter_hit()<br/>Check date, align ratio<br/>duplicates, length"]
        PROCESS["_process_single_hit()<br/>Parse mmCIF<br/>Extract features"]
        
        subgraph "Feature Extraction"
            FIND["_find_template_in_pdb()<br/>Match template chain"]
            REALIGN["_realign_pdb_template_to_query()<br/>Align with Kalign"]
            EXTRACT["_extract_template_features()<br/>Map atoms to query indices"]
            CHECK["_check_residue_distances()<br/>Validate CA-CA distances"]
        end
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Features"
        T_AATYPE["template_aatype<br/>(num_templates, num_res, 22)<br/>float32"]
        T_POS["template_all_atom_positions<br/>(num_templates, num_res, 37, 3)<br/>float32"]
        T_MASK["template_all_atom_mask<br/>(num_templates, num_res, 37)<br/>float32"]
        T_SEQ["template_sequence<br/>(num_templates,)<br/>object"]
        T_DOMAIN["template_domain_names<br/>(num_templates,)<br/>object"]
        T_PROBS["template_sum_probs<br/>(num_templates, 1)<br/>float32"]
    end
    
    HITS --> PREFILT
    QUERY --> PREFILT
    PREFILT -->|valid| PROCESS
    PROCESS --> FIND
    FIND --> REALIGN
    REALIGN --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> CHECK
    CHECK --> T_AATYPE
    CHECK --> T_POS
    CHECK --> T_MASK
    CHECK --> T_SEQ
    CHECK --> T_DOMAIN
    CHECK --> T_PROBS
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/templates.py:826-930](), [openfold/data/templates.py:548-706](), [openfold/data/templates.py:292-364]()

### Template Feature Details

Templates contain structural information extracted from mmCIF files:

| Feature Name | Shape | Type | Description |
|--------------|-------|------|-------------|
| `template_aatype` | `(num_templates, num_res, 22)` | `float32` | One-hot amino acid types (HHBLITS encoding) |
| `template_all_atom_positions` | `(num_templates, num_res, 37, 3)` | `float32` | Atom37 coordinates, aligned to query |
| `template_all_atom_mask` | `(num_templates, num_res, 37)` | `float32` | Mask indicating which atoms are present |
| `template_domain_names` | `(num_templates,)` | `object` | PDB_ID + chain ID (e.g., "4hhb_a") |
| `template_sequence` | `(num_templates,)` | `object` | Aligned template sequence |
| `template_sum_probs` | `(num_templates, 1)` | `float32` | HHSearch sum of probabilities score |

**Sources**: [openfold/data/templates.py:83-90](), [openfold/data/templates.py:93-108]()

### ESM-1b Embeddings (SoloSeq Mode)

When `seqemb_mode=True`, single-sequence embeddings replace MSA features:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "ESM-1b Embedding Generation"
        FASTA["FASTA File"]
        EMB_GEN["EmbeddingGenerator<br/>scripts/precompute_embeddings.py"]
        ESM["ESM-1b Model"]
        EMB_FILE["*.pt file<br/>representations[33]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Feature Processing"
        LOAD["Load *.pt file"]
        EXTRACT["Extract layer 33<br/>representation"]
        DUMMY["Generate dummy MSA<br/>single sequence"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        SEQ_EMB["seq_embedding<br/>(num_res, 1280)<br/>float32"]
        MSA_DUMMY["msa (single-sequence)<br/>(1, num_res)<br/>int32"]
    end
    
    FASTA --> EMB_GEN
    EMB_GEN --> ESM
    ESM --> EMB_FILE
    EMB_FILE --> LOAD
    LOAD --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> SEQ_EMB
    FASTA --> DUMMY
    DUMMY --> MSA_DUMMY
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:849-862](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:284-294](), [run_pretrained_openfold.py:89-97]()

## Input Format Processing

### FASTA Processing

The `process_fasta()` method handles single-chain FASTA inputs:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant DP as DataPipeline
    participant P as Parsers
    participant TF as TemplateFeaturizer
    
    C->>DP: process_fasta(fasta_path, alignment_dir, seqemb_mode)
    DP->>P: parse_fasta(fasta_str)
    P-->>DP: input_sequence, description
    
    DP->>DP: _parse_template_hit_files(alignment_dir)
    DP->>DP: make_sequence_features(sequence, description, num_res)
    
    alt seqemb_mode
        DP->>DP: make_dummy_msa_feats(input_sequence)
        DP->>DP: _process_seqemb_features(alignment_dir)
        Note over DP: Load ESM-1b embeddings
    else normal mode
        DP->>DP: _process_msa_feats(alignment_dir, input_sequence)
        Note over DP: Parse MSA files
    end
    
    DP->>TF: get_templates(input_sequence, hits)
    TF-->>DP: template_features
    
    DP->>C: Return FeatureDict (sequence + MSA/embeddings + templates)
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:864-914]()

### mmCIF Processing

The `process_mmcif()` method processes structural data with alignments:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input"

        ALIGN["alignment_dir"]

        SELECT["Select chain<br/>or use single chain"]
        MMCIF_FEAT["make_mmcif_features()<br/>Extract structure features"]
        SEQ_EXTRACT["Extract input_sequence<br/>from chain_to_seqres"]
        MSA_PROC["_process_msa_feats()<br/>Parse MSA files"]
        TEMPL_PROC["_parse_template_hit_files()<br/>Parse template hits"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Features"
        BASE["Basic sequence features<br/>aatype, residue_index"]
        STRUCT["Structure features<br/>all_atom_positions<br/>all_atom_mask"]
        METADATA["Metadata<br/>resolution<br/>release_date<br/>is_distillation"]
        MSA_F["MSA features"]
        TEMPL_F["Template features"]
    end
    
    MMCIF --> SELECT
    CHAIN --> SELECT
    SELECT --> MMCIF_FEAT
    SELECT --> SEQ_EXTRACT
    MMCIF_FEAT --> BASE
    MMCIF_FEAT --> STRUCT
    MMCIF_FEAT --> METADATA
    ALIGN --> MSA_PROC

    TEMPL_PROC --> TEMPL_F
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:916-999](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:133-166]()

## Monomer vs Multimer Pipeline

The pipeline has different implementations for monomer and multimer predictions:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Monomer Pipeline"
        M_FASTA["Single-chain FASTA"]
        M_ALIGN["Per-sequence alignment<br/>directories"]
        M_DP["DataPipeline"]
        M_FEAT["FeatureDict<br/>single chain"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Multimer Pipeline"
        MM_FASTA["Multi-chain FASTA"]
        MM_ALIGN["Per-sequence alignment<br/>directories"]
        MM_DP["DataPipelineMultimer"]
        MM_MONO["monomer_data_pipeline<br/>DataPipeline"]
        MM_PROC["Process each chain"]
        MM_PAIR["Pair MSAs<br/>add_assembly_features()"]
        MM_FEAT["FeatureDict<br/>multiple chains"]
    end
    
    M_FASTA --> M_ALIGN
    M_ALIGN --> M_DP
    M_DP --> M_FEAT
    
    MM_FASTA --> MM_ALIGN
    MM_ALIGN --> MM_DP
    MM_DP --> MM_MONO
    MM_MONO --> MM_PROC
    MM_PROC --> MM_PAIR
    MM_PAIR --> MM_FEAT
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:706-915](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:916-1161](), [run_pretrained_openfold.py:236-242]()

### Multimer-Specific Processing

The `DataPipelineMultimer` class extends the monomer pipeline:

1. **Per-Chain Processing**: Each chain is processed independently using `monomer_data_pipeline`
2. **Chain Feature Conversion**: `convert_monomer_features()` reshapes features for multimer models
3. **Assembly Features**: `add_assembly_features()` adds chain identity markers (`asym_id`, `sym_id`, `entity_id`)
4. **MSA Pairing**: Uses `pair_and_merge()` to create paired MSAs from UniProt hits

See [Multimer-Specific Processing](#6.4) for detailed information.

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:1048-1161](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:600-624](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:649-691]()

---

## Integration with Inference Script

The inference script (`run_pretrained_openfold.py`) orchestrates the data pipeline:

### Inference Workflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Script as run_pretrained_openfold.py
    participant AR as AlignmentRunner
    participant DP as DataPipeline
    participant FP as FeaturePipeline
    participant Model as AlphaFold Model
    
    Script->>Script: Parse command-line args
    Script->>Script: Create DataPipeline with TemplateFeaturizer
    
    loop For each FASTA file
        Script->>AR: precompute_alignments(tags, seqs, alignment_dir)
        AR-->>Script: Alignments written to disk
        
        Script->>DP: generate_feature_dict(tags, seqs, alignment_dir)
        DP-->>Script: raw_feature_dict
        
        Script->>FP: process_features(feature_dict, mode='predict')
        FP-->>Script: processed_feature_dict (with recycling dims)
        
        Script->>Model: forward(processed_feature_dict)
        Model-->>Script: predictions
        
        Script->>Script: prep_output() -> Protein object
        Script->>Script: Write PDB/mmCIF + optional relaxation
    end
```

**Sources**: [run_pretrained_openfold.py:177-395]()

### Key Functions in Inference

| Function | Location | Purpose |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `precompute_alignments()` | [run_pretrained_openfold.py:63-123]() | Create or load MSA/template alignments |
| `generate_feature_dict()` | [run_pretrained_openfold.py:129-170]() | Call DataPipeline to create FeatureDict |
| `FeaturePipeline.process_features()` | Used via import | Apply data transforms and prepare for model |

```mermaid
graph LR

    PARSE["Parse files<br/>extract sequences"]
    GROUP["Group by sequence<br/>deduplicate"]
    ALIGN["Run AlignmentRunner<br/>for each group"]
    OUTPUT["Output Directory<br/>per-chain subdirs"]
    
    INPUT --> PARSE
    PARSE --> GROUP
    GROUP --> ALIGN
    ALIGN --> OUTPUT
```

**Usage**: Precompute alignments for training datasets to avoid redundant alignment searches.

Create metadata cache for mmCIF files:

```mermaid
graph LR
    MMCIF_DIR["mmCIF Directory"]

    CACHE["JSON Cache File"]
    
    MMCIF_DIR --> PARSE
    PARSE --> EXTRACT

```

**Usage**: Speed up dataset filtering by caching mmCIF metadata without parsing full structures every time.

## Error Handling and Edge Cases

The data pipeline includes extensive error handling:

### Template Processing Errors

| Error Class | Cause | Handling |
|-------------|-------|----------|
| `DateError` | Template released after cutoff | Filtered in prefilter, logged |
| `AlignRatioError` | Insufficient alignment coverage | Filtered in prefilter, logged |
| `DuplicateError` | Template is subsequence of query | Filtered in prefilter, logged |
| `LengthError` | Template too short (< 10 residues) | Filtered in prefilter, logged |
| `SequenceNotInTemplateError` | Chain not found in mmCIF | Triggers realignment attempt |
| `QueryToTemplateAlignError` | Realignment failed or < 90% identity | Template skipped, warning logged |
| `NoAtomDataInTemplateError` | Missing atom coordinates | Template skipped, warning logged |
| `TemplateAtomMaskAllZerosError` | All atoms masked | Template skipped, warning logged |

**Sources**: [openfold/data/templates.py:62-81](), [openfold/data/templates.py:220-289](), [openfold/data/templates.py:780-816]()

### Empty MSA Handling

When no MSA files are found, the pipeline creates a dummy single-sequence MSA:

```python
# If no MSAs found and input_sequence provided
msa_data["dummy"] = make_dummy_msa_obj(input_sequence)
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:813-830](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:284-294]()

---

## Performance Considerations

### MSA Size Limits

The `AlignmentRunner` accepts parameters to limit MSA sizes:

- `uniref_max_hits`: Default 10,000 sequences
- `mgnify_max_hits`: Default 5,000 sequences  
- `uniprot_max_hits`: Default 50,000 sequences (multimer)

These limits prevent excessive MSA sizes that would slow down downstream processing.

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:349-351](), [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:413-415]()

### Parallelization

The `AlignmentRunner` uses the `no_cpus` parameter to parallelize external tool execution (jackhmmer, hhblits). The `precompute_alignments.py` script further parallelizes across multiple sequences using threading.

**Sources**: [openfold/data/data_pipeline.py:418-420](), [scripts/precompute_alignments.py:223-231]()

### File Caching

The template extraction system uses `functools.lru_cache` on file reading operations to avoid redundant disk I/O when multiple hits reference the same mmCIF file:

```python
@functools.lru_cache(16, typed=False)
def _read_file(path):
    with open(path, 'r') as f:
        file_data = f.read()
    return file_data
```

**Sources**: [openfold/data/templates.py:818-823]()

---

# Data Transforms and Augmentation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the data transformation system in OpenFold, which converts raw protein features into model-ready tensors. These transformations handle normalization, augmentation, masking, clustering, and structural feature extraction. The transforms are applied after initial feature generation (see [Data Pipeline and Feature Generation](#6.1)) and before features are fed to the model.

The primary implementation is in [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:1-1266](), with pipeline composition logic in [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:1-213](). For MSA-specific processing, see [MSA and Template Processing](#6.3).

---

## Transform Categories Overview

Data transforms in OpenFold are organized into six functional categories:

```mermaid
graph TB
    RAW["Raw FeatureDict<br/>from DataPipeline"]
    
    subgraph "Transform Categories"
        NORM["Type Conversion & Normalization<br/>cast_to_64bit_ints<br/>correct_msa_restypes<br/>fix_templates_aatype<br/>squeeze_features"]
        
        SAMPLE["MSA Sampling & Filtering<br/>sample_msa<br/>crop_extra_msa<br/>block_delete_msa<br/>randomly_replace_msa_with_unknown"]
        
        MASK["BERT-style MSA Masking<br/>make_hhblits_profile<br/>make_masked_msa"]
        
        CLUSTER["MSA Clustering<br/>nearest_neighbor_clusters<br/>summarize_clusters"]
        
        STRUCT["Structural Features<br/>make_atom14_masks<br/>make_atom14_positions<br/>atom37_to_frames<br/>atom37_to_torsion_angles<br/>make_pseudo_beta"]
        
        SHAPE["Shape Processing<br/>random_crop_to_size<br/>make_fixed_size<br/>crop_templates"]
    end
    
    FEAT["Feature Assembly<br/>make_msa_feat<br/>make_seq_mask<br/>make_msa_mask"]
    
    MODEL["Model-Ready Tensors<br/>msa_feat, target_feat<br/>templates, atom14, etc."]
    
    RAW --> NORM
    NORM --> SAMPLE
    SAMPLE --> MASK
    MASK --> CLUSTER
    CLUSTER --> SHAPE
    SHAPE --> STRUCT
    STRUCT --> FEAT
    FEAT --> MODEL
```

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:1-1266](), [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:23-154]()

---

## Type Conversion and Normalization

These transforms ensure data types and residue encodings are consistent with OpenFold's internal representations.

### cast_to_64bit_ints

Converts all `int32` tensors to `int64` to maintain consistency across the codebase.

```mermaid
graph LR
    IN["protein dict<br/>various int32 tensors"]
    FUNC["cast_to_64bit_ints"]
    OUT["protein dict<br/>all ints are int64"]
    
    IN --> FUNC
    FUNC --> OUT
```

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:46-52]()

### correct_msa_restypes

Maps MSA amino acid encodings from HHblits format to OpenFold's internal ordering using `rc.MAP_HHBLITS_AATYPE_TO_OUR_AATYPE`.

| Input | Output |
|-------|--------|
| `protein["msa"]` - MSA in HHblits encoding | `protein["msa"]` - MSA in OpenFold encoding |
| Profile features (if present) | Reordered profile features |

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:107-129]()

### fix_templates_aatype

Converts template amino acid types from one-hot encoding to indices, then maps from HHblits to OpenFold ordering.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:89-104]()

### squeeze_features

Removes singleton dimensions from features like `domain_name`, `msa`, `num_alignments`, `seq_length`, and `sequence`. Also converts one-hot `aatype` to indices.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:132-160]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:46-160](), [openfold/np/residue_constants.py]()

---

## MSA Sampling and Filtering

These transforms control MSA size through sampling, cropping, and augmentation strategies.

### sample_msa

Randomly samples up to `max_seq` sequences from the MSA while always keeping the query sequence (index 0) first. Remaining sequences are optionally stored with `extra_` prefix.

```mermaid
graph TB
    MSA["MSA with N sequences<br/>shape: [N, L]"]
    
    KEEP["Keep query sequence<br/>index 0"]
    SHUFFLE["Shuffle remaining<br/>indices 1 to N-1"]
    SELECT["Select first max_seq<br/>sequences total"]
    
    MAIN["Main MSA<br/>shape: [min(max_seq, N), L]"]
    EXTRA["Extra MSA (if keep_extra)<br/>shape: [N - min(max_seq, N), L]"]
    
    MSA --> KEEP
    MSA --> SHUFFLE
    SHUFFLE --> SELECT
    KEEP --> MAIN
    SELECT --> MAIN
    SELECT --> EXTRA
```

**Function Signature:** `sample_msa(protein, max_seq, keep_extra, seed=None)`

**Key Parameters:**
- `max_seq`: Maximum number of sequences to retain
- `keep_extra`: If `True`, stores overflow in `extra_msa`, `extra_deletion_matrix`, etc.
- `seed`: Random seed for reproducibility (used in non-resampling recycling mode)

**MSA Feature Names:** Defined in [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:36-43]()
```python
MSA_FEATURE_NAMES = [
    "msa", "deletion_matrix", "msa_mask", 
    "msa_row_mask", "bert_mask", "true_msa",
]
```

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:185-213]()

### crop_extra_msa

Randomly crops `extra_msa` to a maximum size. Used after clustering to limit memory usage.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:228-239]()

### delete_extra_msa

Removes all `extra_*` features from the protein dictionary. Used when extra MSA is not needed.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:242-246]()

### block_delete_msa

Training-only augmentation that randomly deletes contiguous blocks of MSA sequences to encourage robustness.

**Configuration Parameters:**
- `msa_fraction_per_block`: Fraction of MSA sequences per block
- `num_blocks`: Number of blocks to delete
- `randomize_num_blocks`: Whether to randomize the number of blocks

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:250-286]()

### randomly_replace_msa_with_unknown

Replaces a random fraction of MSA positions with the unknown amino acid token ('X', index 20) for augmentation. Skips gaps (index 21).

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:163-182]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:185-286](), [tests/test_data_transforms.py:99-138]()

---

## BERT-style MSA Masking

OpenFold uses BERT-style masking during training to predict masked positions, similar to masked language modeling.

### Masking Pipeline

```mermaid
graph TB
    MSA["Original MSA"]
    PROFILE["make_hhblits_profile<br/>Compute amino acid frequencies"]
    
    PROBS["Categorical Probabilities<br/>uniform_prob × random_aa +<br/>profile_prob × hhblits_profile +<br/>same_prob × current_aa +<br/>mask_prob × [MASK]"]
    
    SAMPLE["Sample replacement values<br/>shaped_categorical"]
    
    SELECT["Select positions to mask<br/>sample < replace_fraction"]
    
    APPLY["Apply masking<br/>bert_msa = where(mask_position, sampled, original)"]
    
    OUT["Output:<br/>bert_mask: mask positions<br/>true_msa: original MSA<br/>msa: masked MSA"]
    
    MSA --> PROFILE
    PROFILE --> PROBS
    MSA --> PROBS
    PROBS --> SAMPLE
    SAMPLE --> SELECT
    SELECT --> APPLY
    MSA --> SELECT
    APPLY --> OUT
```

### make_hhblits_profile

Computes per-residue amino acid frequencies across all MSA sequences by averaging one-hot encoded MSA.

**Output:** `protein["hhblits_profile"]` - shape `[num_residues, 22]`

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:439-448]()

### make_masked_msa

Creates BERT-style masked MSA with configurable replacement strategy.

**Function Signature:** `make_masked_msa(protein, config, replace_fraction, seed)`

**Configuration Parameters:**
| Parameter | Purpose | Typical Value |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| `uniform_prob` | Probability of replacing with random AA | 0.1 |
| `profile_prob` | Probability of sampling from profile | 0.1 |
| `same_prob` | Probability of keeping same AA | 0.1 |
| Remaining probability | Replace with [MASK] token (index 22) | 0.7 |

**replace_fraction:** Fraction of positions to mask (typically 0.15)

**Outputs:**
- `protein["bert_mask"]`: Binary mask indicating masked positions
- `protein["true_msa"]`: Original unmasked MSA
- `protein["msa"]`: Masked MSA for input to model

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:451-501]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:439-501](), [tests/test_data_transforms.py:170-186]()

---

## MSA Clustering

Clustering reduces extra MSA sequences into summary statistics, improving computational efficiency.

### nearest_neighbor_clusters

Assigns each `extra_msa` sequence to its nearest neighbor in the main MSA using weighted Hamming distance.

```mermaid
graph TB
    MSA["Main MSA<br/>shape: [N_msa, L]"]
    EXTRA["Extra MSA<br/>shape: [N_extra, L]"]
    
    ONEHOT["Convert to one-hot<br/>shape: [*, L, 23]"]
    
    WEIGHT["Apply weights:<br/>21 AAs: weight 1.0<br/>Gap: gap_agreement_weight<br/>Unknown: weight 0.0"]
    
    MATMUL["Compute agreement<br/>matmul(extra_one_hot, sample_one_hot.T)<br/>shape: [N_extra, N_msa]"]
    
    ARGMAX["Assign to nearest<br/>argmax along N_msa dimension"]
    
    OUT["extra_cluster_assignment<br/>shape: [N_extra]"]
    
    MSA --> ONEHOT
    EXTRA --> ONEHOT
    ONEHOT --> WEIGHT
    WEIGHT --> MATMUL
    MATMUL --> ARGMAX
    ARGMAX --> OUT
```

**Key Parameter:** `gap_agreement_weight` (default 0.0) - weight given to gap positions in agreement calculation

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:289-323]()

### summarize_clusters

Computes cluster statistics: amino acid profile and average deletion values for each main MSA position.

**Algorithm:**
1. Use `unsorted_segment_sum` to aggregate extra MSA sequences by cluster assignment
2. Compute `cluster_profile`: one-hot frequencies including cluster center
3. Compute `cluster_deletion_mean`: average deletion matrix values

**Outputs:**
- `protein["cluster_profile"]`: shape `[N_msa, L, 23]`
- `protein["cluster_deletion_mean"]`: shape `[N_msa, L]`

**Helper Function:** `unsorted_segment_sum` - [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:326-350]()

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:353-376]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:289-376](), [tests/test_data_transforms.py:140-149]()

---

## Structural Feature Extraction

These transforms convert atom37 coordinates into various geometric representations needed for training and loss computation.

### Atom Representation Conversions

```mermaid
graph TB
    ATOM37["all_atom_positions<br/>all_atom_mask<br/>37 atoms per residue<br/>includes hydrogens"]
    
    ATOM14["atom14_gt_positions<br/>atom14_gt_exists<br/>14 heavy atoms per residue<br/>denser representation"]
    
    FRAMES["rigidgroups_gt_frames<br/>rigidgroups_gt_exists<br/>8 rigid groups per residue<br/>backbone + 4 chi angles"]
    
    TORSION["torsion_angles_sin_cos<br/>torsion_angles_mask<br/>7 angles: omega, phi, psi, 4 chis"]
    
    PSEUDO["pseudo_beta<br/>pseudo_beta_mask<br/>CB position (CA for glycine)"]
    
    ATOM37 --> ATOM14
    ATOM37 --> FRAMES
    ATOM37 --> TORSION
    ATOM37 --> PSEUDO
    
    ATOM14 -.alternative positions.-> ALT14["atom14_alt_gt_positions<br/>atom14_alt_gt_exists<br/>handles ambiguous atoms"]
    FRAMES -.alternative frames.-> ALTFRAMES["rigidgroups_alt_gt_frames<br/>handles symmetric sidechains"]
    TORSION -.alternative angles.-> ALTTORSION["alt_torsion_angles_sin_cos<br/>accounts for pi-periodicity"]
```

### make_atom14_masks

Creates mapping tensors between atom37 and atom14 representations.

**Outputs:**

| Feature | Shape | Description |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| `atom14_atom_exists` | `[N_res, 14]` | Mask for which atom14 positions exist for each residue type |
| `residx_atom14_to_atom37` | `[N_res, 14]` | Mapping from atom14 to atom37 indices |
| `residx_atom37_to_atom14` | `[N_res, 37]` | Mapping from atom37 to atom14 indices |
| `atom37_atom_exists` | `[N_res, 37]` | Mask for which atom37 positions exist for each residue type |

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:607-678]()

### make_atom14_positions

Converts atom37 ground truth positions to atom14 representation using the mappings from `make_atom14_masks`. Handles ambiguous atom naming for 7 residue types (Arg, Asp, Glu, Leu, Phe, Tyr, Val).

**Key Features:**
- Uses `batched_gather` to map atom37 positions to atom14
- Creates alternative positions for ambiguous atoms using renaming matrices
- Marks ambiguous atoms with `atom14_atom_is_ambiguous`

**Outputs:**
- `atom14_gt_positions`, `atom14_gt_exists`: Main ground truth
- `atom14_alt_gt_positions`, `atom14_alt_gt_exists`: Alternative ground truth for ambiguous atoms

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:692-792]()

### atom37_to_frames

Computes rigid body frames for 8 rigid groups per residue: backbone, carbonyl, and up to 4 chi angle groups.

**Rigid Groups:**
- Group 0: Backbone (N-CA-C frame)
- Group 3: Carbonyl (CA-C-O frame)
- Groups 4-7: Chi angle frames (when defined for the residue type)

**Algorithm:**
1. Gather base atoms for each rigid group from atom37 positions
2. Use `Rigid.from_3_points` to construct frames from three points
3. Handle frame ambiguity for symmetric sidechains (e.g., Asp, Glu)

**Outputs:**
- `rigidgroups_gt_frames`: shape `[N_res, 8, 4, 4]` (4x4 transformation matrices)
- `rigidgroups_gt_exists`: frame validity mask
- `rigidgroups_group_exists`: group existence mask
- `rigidgroups_alt_gt_frames`: alternative frames for ambiguous groups

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:795-963]()

### atom37_to_torsion_angles

Computes backbone and sidechain torsion angles (omega, phi, psi, chi1-chi4) from atom37 coordinates.

**Torsion Angles:**
1. Pre-omega: C(i-1) - CA(i-1) - C(i-1) - N(i)
2. Phi: C(i-1) - N(i) - CA(i) - C(i)
3. Psi: N(i) - CA(i) - C(i) - N(i+1)
4. Chi1-4: Sidechain torsion angles (residue-dependent)

**Algorithm:**
1. Gather atom positions for each torsion angle
2. Construct rigid frames from first three atoms
3. Transform fourth atom to frame coordinates
4. Extract sin/cos from transformed coordinates
5. Create alternative angles for symmetric groups

**Outputs:**
- `torsion_angles_sin_cos`: shape `[N_res, 7, 2]`
- `alt_torsion_angles_sin_cos`: alternative angles for pi-periodic chis
- `torsion_angles_mask`: validity mask

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:993-1159]()

### make_pseudo_beta

Creates pseudo-beta positions (CB for all residues except glycine, which uses CA).

**Function Signature:** `make_pseudo_beta(protein, prefix="")`

The `prefix` parameter allows this to work on either target features (`prefix=""`) or template features (`prefix="template_"`).

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:408-420]()

### Additional Structural Helpers

**get_backbone_frames:** Extracts backbone frames from `rigidgroups_gt_frames[..., 0, :, :]`

**get_chi_angles:** Extracts chi angles from `torsion_angles_sin_cos[..., 3:, :]`

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:1162-1179]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:388-1179](), [openfold/utils/rigid_utils.py](), [openfold/np/residue_constants.py]()

---

## Cropping and Padding

These transforms adjust tensor sizes for batching and fixed-size training.

### random_crop_to_size

Randomly crops the protein to a specified size along the residue dimension. Used during training to handle variable-length proteins.

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["Input protein<br/>seq_length: L<br/>num_templates: T"]
    
    CHECK{"L > crop_size?"}
    
    NOCROP["Keep as is"]
    
    CROP["Random cropping"]
    
    subgraph "Cropping Logic"
        CALC["Calculate crop parameters:<br/>num_res_crop_size = min(L, crop_size)<br/>num_templates_crop_size = min(T, max_templates)"]
        
        SEED["Use seed for reproducibility<br/>important for ensemble consistency"]
        
        RAND["Random crop start:<br/>num_res_crop_start in [0, L - crop_size]"]
        
        TEMPLATE{"subsample_templates?"}
        
        TRAND["Random template permutation<br/>and crop"]
        
        TCROP["Sequential template crop"]
        
        APPLY["Apply slices to all features<br/>using shape_schema"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT["Cropped protein<br/>seq_length: crop_size<br/>num_templates: max_templates"]
    
    INPUT --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|No| NOCROP
    CHECK -->|Yes| CROP
    NOCROP --> OUTPUT
    
    CROP --> CALC
    CALC --> SEED
    SEED --> RAND
    RAND --> TEMPLATE
    TEMPLATE -->|Yes| TRAND
    TEMPLATE -->|No| TCROP
    TRAND --> APPLY
    TCROP --> APPLY
    APPLY --> OUTPUT
```

**Key Parameters:**
- `crop_size`: Target number of residues
- `max_templates`: Maximum number of templates to keep
- `shape_schema`: Dictionary defining expected dimensions for each feature
- `subsample_templates`: Whether to randomly permute templates before cropping
- `seed`: Random seed for ensemble consistency

**Special Handling:**
- Always crops along `NUM_RES` dimension when present
- For template features, crops along template dimension (axis 0)
- Uses `use_clamped_fape` flag to control crop positioning (for distillation)

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:1182-1265]()

### make_fixed_size

Pads features to fixed sizes for batching. Uses `shape_schema` to determine which dimensions to pad.

**Pad Size Mapping:**
| Schema Dimension | Pad Size | Description |
|-----------------|----------|-------------|
| `NUM_RES` | `num_res` | Number of residues |
| `NUM_MSA_SEQ` | `msa_cluster_size` | Number of MSA sequences |
| `NUM_EXTRA_SEQ` | `extra_msa_size` | Number of extra MSA sequences |
| `NUM_TEMPLATES` | `num_templates` | Number of templates |

**Algorithm:**
1. For each feature, match shape to schema
2. Compute padding needed: `pad_size[i] = pad_size_map[schema[i]] or original_size[i]`
3. Apply padding using `torch.nn.functional.pad`
4. Reshape to target size

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:504-540]()

### crop_templates

Simple template cropping to a maximum number, applied when not using fixed-size mode.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:599-604]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:504-540, 599-604, 1182-1265](), [openfold/config.py]()

---

## Feature Assembly

Final assembly transforms that create model-ready feature tensors.

### make_msa_feat

Concatenates MSA-related features into unified `msa_feat` and `target_feat` tensors.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Features"
        MSA["msa<br/>shape: [N_msa, L]"]
        DEL["deletion_matrix<br/>shape: [N_msa, L]"]
        AATYPE["aatype<br/>shape: [L]"]
        BREAK["between_segment_residues<br/>shape: [L]"]
        CLUSTER["cluster_profile (optional)<br/>cluster_deletion_mean (optional)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Target Features (22 dims)"
        T1["has_break: [L, 1]<br/>clip(between_segment_residues, 0, 1)"]
        T2["aatype_1hot: [L, 21]<br/>one-hot encoding"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MSA Features (25 or 49 dims)"
        M1["msa_1hot: [N_msa, L, 23]<br/>one-hot with gap and mask"]
        M2["has_deletion: [N_msa, L, 1]<br/>clip(deletion_matrix, 0, 1)"]
        M3["deletion_value: [N_msa, L, 1]<br/>atan(deletion_matrix / 3) × (2/π)"]
        M4["cluster_profile: [N_msa, L, 23]<br/>if clustering enabled"]
        M5["deletion_mean_value: [N_msa, L, 1]<br/>if clustering enabled"]
    end
    
    CONCAT1["torch.cat<br/>→ target_feat"]
    CONCAT2["torch.cat<br/>→ msa_feat"]
    
    OUTPUT["protein['target_feat']: [L, 22]<br/>protein['msa_feat']: [N_msa, L, 25 or 49]"]
    
    AATYPE --> T2
    BREAK --> T1
    T1 --> CONCAT1
    T2 --> CONCAT1
    
    MSA --> M1
    DEL --> M2
    DEL --> M3
    M1 --> CONCAT2
    M2 --> CONCAT2
    M3 --> CONCAT2
    
    CLUSTER --> M4
    CLUSTER --> M5
    M4 --> CONCAT2
    M5 --> CONCAT2
    
    CONCAT1 --> OUTPUT
    CONCAT2 --> OUTPUT
```

**Feature Dimensions:**
- **Without clustering:** `msa_feat` is 25-dimensional (23 + 1 + 1)
- **With clustering:** `msa_feat` is 49-dimensional (23 + 1 + 1 + 23 + 1)
- **target_feat:** Always 22-dimensional (1 + 21)

**Extra MSA Features:**
If `extra_deletion_matrix` is present, also creates:
- `extra_has_deletion`
- `extra_deletion_value`

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:543-591]()

### Mask Creation Helpers

**make_seq_mask:** Creates sequence mask (all ones, later zero-padded)

**make_msa_mask:** Creates MSA masks (`msa_mask` and `msa_row_mask`)

**make_template_mask:** Creates template mask from template_aatype shape

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:61-72, 379-385]()

### select_feat

Filters protein dictionary to include only specified features, used before cropping.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:594-596]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:61-72, 379-385, 543-596]()

---

## Transform Pipeline Composition

Transforms are organized into two pipelines: non-ensembled (applied once) and ensembled (applied per recycling iteration).

### Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    RAW["Raw FeatureDict"]
    
    subgraph "Non-Ensembled Pipeline (Applied Once)"
        NE1["cast_to_64bit_ints"]
        NE2["correct_msa_restypes"]
        NE3["squeeze_features"]
        NE4["make_seq_mask<br/>make_msa_mask<br/>make_hhblits_profile"]
        NE5["Template processing<br/>(if use_templates):<br/>fix_templates_aatype<br/>make_template_mask<br/>make_pseudo_beta('template_')"]
        NE6["make_atom14_masks"]
        NE7["Supervised features<br/>(if training):<br/>make_atom14_positions<br/>atom37_to_frames<br/>atom37_to_torsion_angles<br/>make_pseudo_beta('')<br/>get_backbone_frames<br/>get_chi_angles"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ensembled Pipeline (Per Recycling Iteration)"
        E1["block_delete_msa<br/>(training only)"]
        E2["sample_msa<br/>(keep_extra=True)"]
        E3["make_masked_msa<br/>(training only)"]
        E4["nearest_neighbor_clusters<br/>summarize_clusters<br/>(if msa_cluster_features)"]
        E5["crop_extra_msa or<br/>delete_extra_msa"]
        E6["make_msa_feat"]
        E7["Fixed-size mode:<br/>select_feat<br/>random_crop_to_size<br/>make_fixed_size"]
        E8["Variable-size mode:<br/>crop_templates"]
    end
    
    STACK["Stack along<br/>recycling dimension"]
    
    MODEL["Model Input Tensors<br/>shape: [..., num_recycling + 1]"]
    
    RAW --> NE1
    NE1 --> NE2
    NE2 --> NE3
    NE3 --> NE4
    NE4 --> NE5
    NE5 --> NE6
    NE6 --> NE7
    
    NE7 --> E1
    E1 --> E2
    E2 --> E3
    E3 --> E4
    E4 --> E5
    E5 --> E6
    E6 --> E7
    E7 --> E8
    
    E8 --> STACK
    STACK --> MODEL
```

### nonensembled_transform_fns

Builds the non-ensembled pipeline based on configuration.

**Function:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:23-67]()

**Pipeline Steps:**
1. Type conversion and normalization
2. MSA masking setup
3. Template processing (if enabled)
4. Structural feature extraction (if supervised)

**Configuration Dependencies:**
- `common_cfg.use_templates`: Enable template processing
- `common_cfg.use_template_torsion_angles`: Add template torsion angles
- `mode_cfg.supervised`: Add ground truth structural features

### ensembled_transform_fns

Builds the ensembled pipeline that is applied per recycling iteration.

**Function:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:70-154]()

**Pipeline Steps:**

| Step | Condition | Transforms |
|------|-----------|------------|
| MSA augmentation | `mode_cfg.block_delete_msa` | `block_delete_msa` |
| MSA sampling | Always | `sample_msa` with seed control |
| BERT masking | `"masked_msa" in common_cfg` | `make_masked_msa` |
| Clustering | `common_cfg.msa_cluster_features` | `nearest_neighbor_clusters`, `summarize_clusters` |
| Extra MSA cropping | Always | `crop_extra_msa` or `delete_extra_msa` |
| Feature assembly | Always | `make_msa_feat` |
| Shape processing | `mode_cfg.fixed_size` | `select_feat`, `random_crop_to_size`, `make_fixed_size` |
| Template cropping | Not fixed-size | `crop_templates` |

**Key Configuration Parameters:**
- `max_msa_clusters`: Main MSA size
- `max_extra_msa`: Extra MSA size (for clustering)
- `max_templates`: Number of templates
- `crop_size`: Residue crop size (fixed-size mode)
- `resample_msa_in_recycling`: Whether to resample MSA each iteration

### Ensemble Seed Control

Ensemble seed determines randomness across recycling iterations:

```python
ensemble_seed = random.randint(0, torch.iinfo(torch.int32).max)

msa_seed = None
if not common_cfg.resample_msa_in_recycling:
    msa_seed = ensemble_seed
```

If `resample_msa_in_recycling=False`, all recycling iterations see the same MSA sampling. This is the typical setting.

### process_tensors_from_config

Main entry point that composes both pipelines and applies them to create model inputs.

**Function:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:157-194]()

**Algorithm:**
1. Generate ensemble seed
2. Apply non-ensembled transforms once
3. Determine number of recycling iterations
4. Apply ensembled transforms for each iteration
5. Stack results along new ensemble dimension

**Output:** Dictionary with all features stacked along final dimension `[..., num_recycling + 1]`

**Sources:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:23-194]()

---

## Utility Functions and Helpers

### curry1

Decorator that enables partial function application, allowing transforms to be configured with parameters before being applied to data.

```python
@curry1
def sample_msa(protein, max_seq, keep_extra, seed=None):
    # Function body
    
# Usage:
transform = sample_msa(max_seq=512, keep_extra=True)
protein = transform(protein)
```

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:75-81]()

### make_one_hot

Converts integer tensor to one-hot encoding.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:55-58]()

### shaped_categorical

Samples from categorical distribution while preserving tensor shape.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:429-436]()

### unsorted_segment_sum

Aggregates tensor values by segment IDs, used in clustering. Similar to TensorFlow's `tf.unsorted_segment_sum`.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:326-350]()

### compose

Composes a list of functions into a single function, applying them sequentially.

**Implementation:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:197-201]()

**Sources:** [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:55-81, 326-350, 429-436](), [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:197-201]()

---

## Training vs. Inference Differences

Transforms are applied differently during training and inference based on configuration:

| Transform | Training | Inference | Controlled By |
|-----------|----------|-----------|---------------|
| `block_delete_msa` | ✓ | ✗ | `mode_cfg.block_delete_msa` |
| `make_masked_msa` | ✓ | ✗ | `"masked_msa" in common_cfg` |
| Structural features | ✓ | ✗ | `mode_cfg.supervised` |
| Fixed-size padding | ✓ | ✗ | `mode_cfg.fixed_size` |
| Random cropping | ✓ | ✗ | `mode_cfg.fixed_size` |
| MSA resampling | Configurable | ✗ | `common_cfg.resample_msa_in_recycling` |

**Training Mode:** [openfold/config.py]() defines `train` mode configuration
- Supervised features enabled
- Fixed-size batching with random cropping
- MSA augmentation (masking, block deletion)
- Typically smaller `max_msa_clusters` (128-512)

**Inference Mode:** [openfold/config.py]() defines `eval` mode configuration  
- No supervised features
- Variable-size (no cropping/padding)
- No MSA augmentation
- Can use larger `max_msa_clusters` (up to 5120)

**Sources:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:23-154](), [openfold/config.py]()

---

## Example Transform Sequences

### Training Transform Sequence

```
Raw Features
    ↓ cast_to_64bit_ints
    ↓ correct_msa_restypes
    ↓ squeeze_features
    ↓ make_seq_mask, make_msa_mask, make_hhblits_profile
    ↓ fix_templates_aatype (if templates)
    ↓ make_atom14_masks
    ↓ make_atom14_positions, atom37_to_frames, atom37_to_torsion_angles
    ↓ make_pseudo_beta, get_backbone_frames, get_chi_angles
── [Ensembled per iteration] ──
    ↓ block_delete_msa (stochastic)
    ↓ sample_msa (keep_extra=True)
    ↓ make_masked_msa (BERT masking)
    ↓ nearest_neighbor_clusters, summarize_clusters
    ↓ crop_extra_msa
    ↓ make_msa_feat
    ↓ select_feat, random_crop_to_size
    ↓ make_fixed_size (pad to batch size)
    ↓ [Stack along recycling dimension]
Model Input
```

### Inference Transform Sequence

```
Raw Features
    ↓ cast_to_64bit_ints
    ↓ correct_msa_restypes
    ↓ squeeze_features
    ↓ make_seq_mask, make_msa_mask, make_hhblits_profile
    ↓ fix_templates_aatype (if templates)
    ↓ make_atom14_masks
── [Ensembled per iteration] ──
    ↓ sample_msa (keep_extra=True, fixed seed)
    ↓ nearest_neighbor_clusters, summarize_clusters
    ↓ crop_extra_msa
    ↓ make_msa_feat
    ↓ crop_templates
    ↓ [Stack along recycling dimension]
Model Input
```

**Sources:** [openfold/data/input_pipeline.py:23-194](), [openfold/data/data_transforms.py:1-1266]()

# Page: MSA and Template Processing

# MSA and Template Processing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>
